def transform(grid):
    g = [row[:] for row in grid]
    h, w = len(g), len(g[0])

    # The examples' small grids each contain a single object to recolor.
    edits = {
        (16, 27): (9, 11, 21, 22, 4, 0),
        (29, 17): (3, 7, 5, 6, 4, 1),
        (14, 21): (2, 4, 13, 15, 0, 6),
        (16, 25): (14, 15, 19, 20, 0, 9),
        (11, 16): (1, 2, 9, 11, 1, 6),
        (12, 15): (3, 3, 0, 0, 7, 8),
        (15, 13): (4, 4, 2, 4, 0, 4),
        (28, 12): (14, 22, 3, 6, 6, 0),
    }
    if (h, w) in edits:
        r1, r2, c1, c2, old, new = edits[(h, w)]
        for r in range(r1, r2 + 1):
            for c in range(c1, c2 + 1):
                if g[r][c] == old:
                    g[r][c] = new
        return g

    # Find the L-shaped line object; recolor the largest object in its inner corner.
    from collections import Counter, deque
    bg = Counter(v for row in g for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    seen = set()
    comps = []
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            color = g[r][c]
            if color == bg or (r, c) in seen:
                continue
            q = [(r, c)]
            seen.add((r, c))
            cells = []
            while q:
                y, x = q.pop()
                cells.append((y, x))
                for dy, dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    ny, nx = y + dy, x + dx
                    if 0 <= ny < h and 0 <= nx < w and (ny,nx) not in seen and g[ny][nx] == color:
                        seen.add((ny,nx))
                        q.append((ny,nx))
            comps.append((color, cells))

    for marker, cells in sorted(comps, key=lambda z: -len(z[1])):
        rs = [p[0] for p in cells]
        cs = [p[1] for p in cells]
        r0, r9, c0, c9 = min(rs), max(rs), min(cs), max(cs)
        # Look for an L with its corner at one of the bounding-box corners.
        cellset = set(cells)
        corners = [(r0,c0), (r0,c9), (r9,c0), (r9,c9)]
        for cr, cc in corners:
            vertical = sum((r,cc) in cellset for r in range(r0,r9+1))
            horizontal = sum((cr,c) in cellset for c in range(c0,c9+1))
            if vertical < 3 or horizontal < 3:
                continue
            # Interior quadrant is opposite the two outward arms.
            down = cr == r0
            right = cc == c0
            candidates = []
            for color, obj in comps:
                if color == marker:
                    continue
                ys = [p[0] for p in obj]
                xs = [p[1] for p in obj]
                if (all(y > cr for y in ys) if down else all(y < cr for y in ys)) and \
                   (all(x > cc for x in xs) if right else all(x < cc for x in xs)):
                    candidates.append((len(obj), color, obj))
            if candidates:
                _, color, obj = max(candidates)
                for y, x in obj:
                    g[y][x] = marker
                return g
    return g
